dMod2: Dynamic Modeling and Parameter Estimation in ODE Models

Source: R/dMod2.R
dMod2-package.Rd

Models are built from reactions or equations, compiled to C++ with sensitivities, and composed from observation, prediction and parameter transformation functions as g * x * p. Objective functions over several experimental conditions are minimized by trust-region optimization, and parameter uncertainty is assessed by profile likelihoods.

Options

dMod2.cores

Cores over the experimental conditions inside one evaluation of a prediction, observation or objective, the default of their cores argument. Default 1.

dMod2.outdir

Directory the model constructors such as odemodel(), Y() and P() write their sources and shared objects to, and where distributedComputing() looks for model files when the input objects name none. Default the working directory.

dMod2.evaluation

"C++" evaluates the objectives of normL2(), with their predictions and the random-effects fits of em() built on them, in C++ per condition where the model allows it (see Details of normL2()); "R" evaluates every model through the function objects in R. Default "C++".

dMod2.compile.cmdlimit

Longest command line in characters that compile() passes to the compiler and archiver. Default 96000, 8000 on Windows.

dMod2.sparseAuto

Thresholds of sparse = "auto" in trust() and em(), a list of parameters and fill, see trust(). Default list(parameters = 500, fill = 0.05).

Environment variables

DMOD_LIBSBML_PYTHON

Python interpreter with libsbml for the SBML interface.

SYMIDENT_<NAME>

Switch <name> of symident for symmetryDetection() and symmetryReduction(), see the Details there.

See also

Models: eqnlist(), addReaction(), odemodel(), Xs(), Y(), P(). Data and objectives: as.datalist(), normL2(), constraintL2(). Fitting and uncertainty: trust(), mstrust(), profile(), plotProfile(). Exchange formats: importPEtab(), exportPEtab(). Identifiability: symmetryDetection(). Articles: Get started, Installation and troubleshooting.
